card.name: Sousta
card.era: Ancient roots (linked to the Pyrrhic war-dance tradition); name from Venetian 'sousta' (carriage spring)
card.tagline: Cretan/Dodecanese couples courtship dance with hopping steps.
card.profile: A Greek folk dance performed at weddings as courtship between partners; prominent in Crete, the Dodecanese and the broader Aegean, and described as second only to the syrtos in commonness. A three-step dance with a 'hopping' bounce - two jump-steps forward, one back - with crossed-over linked hands symbolizing unity. Carries symbolism of romance and marriage; historically a socialisation rite among village youth. Music typically on Cretan or Pontian lyra (or violin), laouto, and mandolin/askomandoura. Named from the Venetian word for a carriage spring, reflecting its bouncy motion (English Wikipedia; IJESSR).
card.insight: The sousta exists in many officially documented island variants (Crete, Rhodes, Halki, Leros, Kalymnos, Karpathos, Kos, Tilos, Samos, Symi); on Rhodes alone scholars record distinct village forms in a peer-reviewed IJESSR study.
